Subject: Cross-organizational MAP & closure anchors (MSA / DPA / Order Form sequencing)

Hi Sara / Lumenica procurement team,

As discussed in last week's demo, I'm sharing an initial mutual action plan (attached) that breaks our go-to-close into three parallel lanes: evaluation acceptance, legal (MSA/DPA redlines), and procurement/order form approval. Key points in this MAP:

- Evaluation acceptance: fixed pilot acceptance criteria and two-week validation window.
- DPA: aim for a baseline DPA with few commercial-dependent addenda so security review can run in parallel.
- MSA + Order Form: draft anchors for payment terms and SLAs; final order form will reference the MSA ID.

I've attached MAP_v1.xlsx with a suggested timeline and owners. Can you confirm: (1) whether Lumenica needs a completed security questionnaire before legal begins redlines, and (2) any internal procurement blackout dates we should avoid?

Proposed high-level timeline (subject to your confirmation):
- Legal redline pass completed: by 2026-11-24
- Procurement review / pricing approval: by 2026-12-02
- Signatures: target week of 2026-12-07 (flexible +/- 1 week)

If that looks reasonable, we can schedule a 30-min alignment call next week to walk the MAP together and lock in owners.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out smoothly.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Cross-organizational MAP & closure anchors (MSA / DPA / Order Form sequencing)

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the MAP. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/security: 

1) Security questionnaire: our InfoSec team usually wants the vendor questionnaire completed (we use the standard Lumenica security questionnaire) before we move to a binding DPA. Can your security contact fill that in this week?

2) DPA expectations: will the baseline DPA include processor-to-processor language, or do you expect a scoped addendum? Our privacy team prefers seeing the full DPA language early to avoid last-minute blockers.

3) Procurement cadence: we have an internal pricing approval window that closes on 2026-11-30 for December commits — if we want to hit your proposed signature week, we need pricing confirmed by 2026-11-29.

We can do a 30-min call — is Tuesday 11/23 or Wednesday 11/24 morning PT possible?

Regards,
Sara Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, Lumenica Health

Hi Sara — thanks for the quick feedback. Answers inline below and next steps: 

1) Security questionnaire: we'll have our security lead complete your questionnaire. Laura (copied) is coordinating the InfoSec response and can drop the completed file into the Drive folder by Monday 11/22 EOD.

2) DPA approach: we typically provide a full DPA first-pass that includes processor-to-processor language where required; however, we can also offer a short-form baseline plus an addendum if that accelerates review. Karthik, our counsel, will propose the minimalist path that balances legal comfort and speed.

3) Pricing deadline: noted — we'll prioritize internal pricing review to try to get you a committed figure by 11/29. I will flag this as critical in our weekly ops sync.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Laura to upload the completed security questionnaire (11/22 EOD)
- Karthik to send DPA/MSA anchor drafts (11/24)
- 30-min alignment call on 11/24 10:00 AM PT (tune if that works for your team)

If the above timeline holds, we should be in good shape for signatures in the week of 12/07.

Cheers,
Vivek
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-organizational MAP & closure anchors (MSA / DPA / Order Form sequencing)

Sara / team — attaching a concise redline set and an MSA anchor draft for your review. Summary of the key items and recommended positions:

Attachments:
- DPA_redlines_20261124.pdf (annotated redlines)
- MSA_anchor_draft_20261124.docx (anchor clauses, payment appendix stub)

Redline highlights / asks for Lumenica legal: 
- Security & data handling: We accept subprocessors with prior notice; recommend adding a 30-day cure period rather than immediate termination for data incidents.
- Liability cap: standard cap at 3x fees with carveouts for gross negligence — if you need a different cap, please propose a counterfigure tied to order value.
- SLA credits: proposing a credits-first remediation path and a 72-hour remediation window.
- Order Form dependencies: the MSA will reference the Order Form ID and the DPA will be incorporated by reference. Please confirm that your procurement team is comfortable with references vs. embedding full DPA text in the order form.

If Lumenica legal can indicate the top 2 items they cannot accept (e.g., liability cap number or data incident cure), we can prioritize negotiation on those points and leave the rest for mutual cleanup.

I'll be on the call Thursday 11/24 at 10:00 AM PT — Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — that set of artifacts and the proposed positions are helpful. Quick responses: 

- Security questionnaire: our InfoSec will accept the completed questionnaire and start an advisory review; that should keep us moving.
- DPA references: procurement prefers the DPA text included as part of the contract package rather than only referenced — we will flag any issues quickly if the text is present.
- Top two legal items: liability cap and SLA remedy timing — we'll push back if the cap is below market for our use case and if SLA windows are tighter than our expectations.

We can hold the 30-min alignment on Friday 11/26 at 9:30 AM PT instead of Thursday, as a couple of our stakeholders are out on Thursday. On timing: internal pricing team is aligned to try for 11/29 pricing confirmation; assuming that, we can target a legal sign-off window by 12/08 and an exec signature pick‑up by 12/09–12/10.

I'll circulate a short agenda and a dial link. Thanks — Sara

Sara Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, Lumenica Health
